title: Ultra-high-purity gas delivery assemblies
plain: Make the pipes and valve panels that carry exceptionally clean gas into chipmaking tools. A microscopic leak or contamination can spoil a manufacturing process, so the product includes proof of cleanliness and traceable testing.
analogy: Like a hospital's sterile fluid line, with each joint tracked and checked before use.
product: Customer-approved inert-gas valve manifold panels, small distribution boxes and orbital-welded tube-spool kits, with test records and installation support.
does: Divides and controls nitrogen or argon supply without adding particles, moisture or avoidable leaks; connects the facility distribution system to a tool's approved interface.
customers: Fab or OSAT facilities engineering teams
Semiconductor tool manufacturers and their subsystem suppliers
Industrial-gas suppliers delivering semiconductor facility projects
whyNow: India has operating semiconductor plants and further approved facilities; these require utilities, extensions and maintenance. Swagelok and Exyte identify high-purity fluid assemblies and off-site utility modules as established supply categories [S1,S4]. This supports a specific vendor-qualification route, not a verified unawarded Indian order book.
firstProduct: An engineered 4- to 8-outlet nitrogen/argon valve manifold family, using customer-approved electropolished stainless tube and diaphragm valves, plus matching prefabricated tube spools. Tube size, pressure and outlet count follow the customer's approved specification.
notIncluded: No gas generation or chemical synthesis; no initial toxic, pyrophoric or corrosive-gas cabinet; no mass-flow-controller or diaphragm-valve manufacture; no complete fab utility EPC. Liquid chemical/PFA assemblies would require a separate qualified process.
entry: Recruit a semiconductor fluid-systems engineering lead and licensed orbital-welding trainer. Qualify first as an assembly supplier to a tool OEM or utility contractor. Obtain the buyer's approved component list and test specification before tooling; obtain the design licence if supplying a partner's proprietary panel.
capacity: Planning assumption: 150-250 small manifold panels and 1,000-2,000 tube spools per year after qualification, one 8-hour shift for 250 days. Weld count and purity-test duration, rather than panel count alone, determine capacity.

budget.basis: INR crore, 2026 pre-feasibility allowances for a leased industrial shell. Recoverable GST, land purchase and new shell construction excluded; freight/installation included in equipment allowances. Working capital separate; no subsidy deducted. Not supplier quotations.

title: Modular cleanrooms and controlled-environment modules
plain: Build rooms that keep airborne dust and operating conditions within an agreed specification. The factory makes wall, ceiling and air-distribution modules and integrates purchased filtration and climate-control equipment at the customer's site.
analogy: A carefully controlled room inside a larger factory, with its own filtered-air circulation.
product: Designed, fabricated and installed modular ISO7/8 suites for electronics assembly, inspection and suitable OSAT support operations, supplied with documented commissioning.
does: Gives the buyer a repeatable controlled environment and a faster modular installation; makes later extensions and maintenance easier when interfaces are designed correctly.
customers: OSAT support/inspection areas with matching environmental requirements
Facility EPC contractors buying a cleanroom package
Precision engineering and photonics assembly laboratories
whyNow: Semiconductor and electronics manufacturing expansion creates controlled-environment work, but the precise classification and process demand vary. Exyte describes off-site modules and coordinated facilities delivery [S4]; Tata Projects has an actual awarded Indian semiconductor facility contract [S5]. This starter product targets smaller repeatable suites rather than treating all fab capex as accessible demand.
firstProduct: A configurable 250-750 sq m ISO7/8 modular suite with steel-skinned panels, sealed doors/windows, a designed ceiling/support system and purchased HEPA/FFU or terminal-filter/HVAC modules. Final class, occupancy state and environmental limits are contractual.
notIncluded: No complete leading-edge wafer-fab EPC, process-gas/chemical distribution, ultra-pure-water plant, lithography vibration-control foundation or semiconductor tool installation. No initial manufacture of HEPA media, chillers or precision FFU motors. Not a pharmaceutical aseptic-validation offer.
entry: Build an engineering-and-fabrication company with an experienced cleanroom HVAC lead, structural reviewer and commissioning team. Start as a specialist subcontractor or direct supplier on a defined room package, with a qualified filtration/HVAC partner. Manufacture panel skins, frames and ducts; outsource coatings and initially buy certified core materials and filters.
capacity: Assume 5-8 customer packages per year after ramp-up, totalling approximately 3,000-5,000 sq m of floor area, on one fabrication shift. Installation crews work at customer sites; square metres are a planning measure, not a booked order forecast.

budget.basis: INR crore, 2026 pre-feasibility estimate for a leased shell; equipment installation included, recoverable GST excluded. Land/new shell excluded; working capital separate; no subsidy deducted. This is a component-fabrication and integration shop, not the cost of building a semiconductor fab.

title: Advanced packaging JV: wafer-level chip-scale packages
plain: Take already fabricated semiconductor wafers and add tiny electrical connections, then test and separate the finished devices. This factory packages chips; it does not fabricate the transistors inside them.
analogy: A specialist finishing and testing plant that turns a wafer of delicate circuits into individually usable components.
product: Qualified 300mm wafer-level chip-scale packaging services with a defined redistribution-layer and solder-interconnect process, wafer probe, singulation and tape-and-reel delivery.
does: Moves a chip's contact points to a board-compatible arrangement and delivers electrically tested compact devices for an anchor chip company.
customers: IDMs outsourcing a qualified wafer-level package
Sensor and mixed-signal chip suppliers with suitable die designs
Established OSAT companies seeking a qualified Indian production partner
whyNow: Semicon2.0 explicitly includes wafer-level chip-scale packaging in its advanced category, subject to a ₹1,000 crore minimum capital investment and technology/financial criteria [S8]. Amkor demonstrates WLCSP as a commercial packaging route for analog, power-management and other chips [S1]. This is a technology-JV opportunity; Indian policy does not provide customer designs, yield know-how or committed utilisation.
firstProduct: One licensed 300mm fan-in WLCSP family for an anchor analog/PMIC or compatible sensor product, initially one or two copper redistribution layers with customer-approved bump pitch and dielectric stack. Begin with one die family and a frozen process design kit.
notIncluded: No leading-edge GPU die fabrication, HBM stacking, silicon interposer/TSV line, hybrid bonding, fan-out panel packaging or universal OSAT portfolio. A small WLCSP package is not a GPU package. Automotive qualification is a later customer-specific programme.
entry: Form a funded Indian JV with an operating packaging technology owner. Secure transfer of the process, package-design rules, customer test programme and experienced resident team. Obtain binding commercial arrangements for wafer supply, qualification lots, liability and capacity before ordering the production line.
capacity: Planning assumption: initially qualify and load 1,000-2,000 300mm wafer-equivalents/month, progressing towards 3,000-5,000 only after bottleneck validation. Operate three shifts, six days/week; device output varies enormously with die size and yield. This is not a vendor-guaranteed nameplate.

budget.basis: INR crore, 2026 pre-feasibility allowance for a long-term leased/leased-to-spec industrial shell. Advanced cleanroom/process fit-out included; purchased land, new base shell/civil construction and recoverable GST excluded. No subsidy deducted. Equipment and technology configuration could materially change this range.

items.name: Process cleanroom, subfab and controlled utilities fit-out
items.note: Clean areas, air handling, gas/chemical distribution, UPW and wastewater handling; shell excluded.

items.name: RDL lithography, deposition and wet-process tools
items.note: Coat/develop, exposure, seed deposition, plating and associated process control.

items.name: Solder-interconnect formation and reflow
items.note: Qualified ball/bump process, cleaning and optical checks.

items.name: Wafer thinning, handling and singulation
items.note: Backgrind, tape/carrier handling, dicing and die sorting.

items.name: Electrical test and probing systems
items.note: Product-specific ATE, probers, probe cards and temperature capability.

items.name: Metrology, failure analysis and reliability lab
items.note: Thickness/overlay inspection, microscopy and package/board-level reliability capability.

items.name: Automation, facility redundancy and information systems
items.note: Material tracking, statistical control, tool integration, critical backups and maintenance spares.

items.name: Technology transfer, engineering and pilot qualification
items.note: Partner transfer, resident expertise, masks and non-saleable pilot lots; not all expenditure necessarily incentive eligible.

items.name: Project integration and contingency
items.note: Installation, schedule/FX allowance and process changes; this is not a quoted contingency requirement.

budget.workingNote: Assumes customer-owned consigned wafers, 12-18-month qualification/ramp reserve, consumables/spares and receivables. Buying wafers or bearing replacement liability can require much more cash; insurance and liability terms must be priced.
budget.landNote: New base building, land, off-site water/power reinforcement and financing interest during construction are additional unless separately agreed in the lease/project structure.
budget.confidence: Low-confidence pre-feasibility range for a JV-scale plant; a licensed process owner must produce the tool list, mass balance and bankable DPR.

site.builtup: Screen 180,000-260,000 sq ft (about 16,720-24,150 sq m), with process clean areas, test, utilities, chemicals, metrology and support separated. A generic warehouse is not automatically suitable.
site.plot: If greenfield: screen 12-20 acres for building, utility/chemical yards, wastewater treatment, access, setbacks and expansion; environmental/industrial siting review controls the final plot.
site.power: Screen 8-15 MVA connected load with engineered quality and backup for critical tools; sanction and feeder reliability unverified.
site.water: Screen 200-600 kL/day raw-water demand before recycling design. Wet-process recipes, tool utilisation, UPW recovery and effluent segregation can change this substantially; obtain a process water balance.
conditions: Require contamination control, vibration review and segregated clean/chemical/service circulation.
Evaluate reliable power/water, permitted chemical storage and effluent treatment before land commitment.
Tumakuru/Mysuru or another Karnataka industrial site is conditional on utilities and talent transport; no location has been pre-approved.

team.why: Own the licensed process, investment gates and customer commitments.
Adapt layouts and test programmes to customer devices.
Stabilise each process module and repair tools.
Control defects, qualification and customer audits.
Operate the line across three shifts.
Keep utilities stable and manage chemical/effluent systems.
Schedule consigned wafers and qualified materials.
Support commercial, workforce and data controls.

teamNote: 335 core people assumed at initial three-shift operation. Partner expatriate/resident specialists may be included among engineering leads; construction/EPC labour and external qualification laboratories are additional. Final staffing follows the licensed line's automation.

machines.name: Coat/develop tracks and exposure tools
machines.quantity: 1 process line; number set by cycle-time model
machines.purpose: Patterns polymer and redistribution features across wafers.
machines.spec: RFQ wafer size, overlay, resist/dielectric compatibility and agreed line/space; do not assume a semiconductor-fab lithography tool is required.

machines.name: Seed-layer deposition and plating tools
machines.purpose: Forms the conductive layer and plated copper features.
machines.spec: Metal stack, uniformity, contamination limits and wafer handling require the licensed process.

machines.name: Wet clean/strip and controlled-cure systems
machines.purpose: Cleans and conditions wafers between process steps.
machines.spec: Chemistry compatibility, exhaust, wastewater segregation and defect-control recipe owned by the process partner.

machines.name: Ball placement/bump formation and reflow
machines.purpose: Creates the solder contacts used by the final board.
machines.spec: Choose one approved interconnect route, pitch and alloy; qualify solder geometry and board reliability.

machines.name: Wafer handling, grinding and dicing cells
machines.purpose: Thins and separates fragile processed wafers.
machines.spec: Wafer thickness, protective handling, die streets and chipping limits set by product design.

machines.name: Wafer probers and product-specific ATE
machines.purpose: Checks electrical behaviour and sorts good devices.
machines.spec: Channel count, voltage/current, temperature and test time depend on the anchor product; high-end GPU test is excluded.

machines.name: Optical/thickness and defect-inspection systems
machines.purpose: Checks alignment, feature dimensions and process defects.
machines.spec: Sampling and automated inspection sensitivity defined through yield engineering.

machines.name: Reliability and failure-analysis instruments
machines.purpose: Investigates failures and validates package/board behaviour.
machines.spec: Customer-agreed qualification plan; include thermal cycling, humidity and cross-section analysis as applicable.

machines.name: Die sort and tape-and-reel systems
machines.purpose: Packs accepted devices with lot traceability.
machines.spec: Pocket/tape design, orientation, inspection and ESD control matched to the shipped product.

process.name: Co-design and incoming wafer release
process.plain: Agree the package before receiving production wafers.
process.detail: Use licensed design rules, incoming wafer maps and customer ownership/liability terms.
process.check: Package design review and incoming wafer acceptance.

process.name: Prepare and coat the wafer
process.plain: Apply the agreed protective/insulating layers.
process.detail: Clean wafer and run the licensed dielectric process without exposing it to uncontrolled contamination.
process.check: Film thickness and defect checks.

process.name: Pattern the connections
process.plain: Define where new electrical routes will sit.
process.detail: Expose/develop the agreed pattern aligned to the original device contacts.
process.check: Overlay and patterned-feature acceptance.

process.name: Build the redistribution metal
process.plain: Create the copper pathways and contact foundations.
process.detail: Run qualified deposition/plating/strip sequence; repeat only for the approved layer count.
process.check: Thickness, resistance and defect control.

process.name: Form solder interconnects
process.plain: Add the contacts that connect to a circuit board.
process.detail: Apply the selected bump/ball route and reflow under the licensed recipe.
process.check: Bump geometry and interconnect checks.

process.name: Thin and electrically test
process.plain: Prepare the wafer and identify good devices.
process.detail: Use the qualified handling/grinding sequence and customer test programme; exact ordering follows the process flow.
process.check: Wafer map, electrical yield and thickness accepted.

process.name: Singulate and pack
process.plain: Separate good devices and protect them for shipment.
process.detail: Dice, inspect and sort according to wafer map; pack with orientation and lot identity.
process.check: Chipping, visual and traceability acceptance.

process.name: Release and monitor reliability
process.plain: Confirm the process remains suitable over time.
process.detail: Execute customer qualification/monitoring plan and investigate excursions before releasing affected lots.
process.check: Customer qualification and controlled lot disposition.

roadmap.gate: Signed partner/customer framework with independent commercial review.

roadmap.actions: Complete tool list, mass balance, site/environmental studies, utility commitments and relevant incentive application.
roadmap.gate: Approved investment decision based on unsubsidised cash needs and conditional sanction terms.

roadmap.actions: Prepare cleanroom/utilities, install and accept equipment, deploy partner engineers and train shifts.
roadmap.gate: Facility/tool acceptance with contamination and measurement controls.

roadmap.actions: Run engineering wafers, package/board reliability and customer audits; fix yield loss.
roadmap.gate: Written production approval for the specific package/product.

roadmap.actions: Increase loaded wafers against orders, track actual cost/yield and add products selectively.
roadmap.gate: Stable customer yield, delivery and utilisation before further technology expansion.

quality.title: Package versus chip performance
quality.detail: Packaging acceptance does not guarantee the customer's circuit design; preserve wafer maps and test responsibility boundaries.

quality.title: Process control
quality.detail: Monitor coating, overlay, metal thickness and defects; customer-qualified process limits govern, not generic brochure specifications.

quality.title: Package and board reliability
quality.detail: Select applicable JEDEC/customer tests for thermal, moisture, mechanical and board-level performance; automotive approval is separate.

quality.title: Traceability and change control
quality.detail: Connect each incoming wafer to tool history, materials, test map and shipped reel; obtain customer permission before approved-process changes.

localisation.part: Package process engineering, RDL/bump processing, test and singulation
localisation.detail: Substantial local semiconductor back-end manufacturing, with transferred process know-how.
Often customer-consigned from an overseas foundry; local packaging does not establish domestic transistor fabrication.

localisation.part: Core process tools, selected chemicals and probe hardware
localisation.detail: Qualified global equipment/materials likely required at launch; spares and export/service access matter.

localisation.part: Facility modules, civil services and suitable mechanical/electrical parts
localisation.detail: Localise to approved specifications without assuming all utility/process components are domestic.

localisation.part: Specialist failure analysis and selected reliability tests
localisation.detail: Use qualified external labs until volume justifies every advanced instrument.

schemes.name: Semicon2.0 advanced ATMP/OSAT
schemes.status: Policy snapshot 19 September 2026; direct-beneficiary application conditional.
schemes.detail: WLCSP is named in the advanced category: ₹1,000 crore minimum capital investment, ₹200 crore qualifying prior revenue including permitted group/JV basis, production-grade owned/licensed technology, and 35% eligible capex support. Total budget above the threshold is not proof every cost is eligible or approval is assured.

schemes.name: Karnataka project package
schemes.detail: Do not assume a blanket central top-up or stack multiple state policies. Budget and finance gross costs until written eligibility, ceiling and payment conditions are established.

network: Use introductions to secure a real technology owner, an anchor fabless/IDM customer and MeitY/ISM application guidance. Ask the partner to commit resident yield engineers and customer introductions, not merely permission to use a brand. MHI access alone does not award a semiconductor subsidy.

risks.risk: Factory starts without enough qualified wafer volume.
risks.response: Stage investment against binding qualification and volume arrangements with sensible cancellation terms.

risks.risk: Yield loss destroys valuable customer wafers.
risks.response: Negotiate consignment/liability terms, insure where possible and require partner-backed process transfer and controlled pilots.

risks.risk: A licence does not include practical production know-how.
risks.response: Specify recipes, design rules, engineering presence, acceptance criteria and ongoing support in the technology agreement.

risks.risk: Utilities or imported tool service delays prevent ramp-up.
risks.response: Secure site service commitments and long-term tool support before construction.

risks.risk: Subsidy approval or reimbursement timing differs from the model.
risks.response: Fund the gross project and treat incentives as conditional, with milestone-based cash-flow scenarios.

first90: Select an actual chip family and its anchor buyer; request wafer maps, electrical-test needs and target package.
Screen two operating WLCSP technology partners for transfer rights and production track record.
Commission a preliminary tool/cycle-time model, utility balance and independently reviewed project economics.
Screen Karnataka sites using power/water/effluent capability before land purchase.
Agree customer-wafer liability, qualification payments and funding structure before scheme-dependent commitments.
